name: Task_2
description:
Study whether sodium silicate shows a resolvable glass transition during cooling and reheating, and assess the effect of thermal history. Start from the supplied molten sodium silicate state at 4000 K in /workspace/structures/melt/liq4000.dat, using read_data. Use the supplied BKS-type Buckingham-Coulomb potential with PPPM electrostatics in LAMMPS, real units, charge atom style, periodic boundaries, and isotropic NPT at zero target pressure. Preserve the supplied atoms, cell, charges, and velocities; do not initialize velocities or reset the step count. Use a 1 fs timestep and 100 fs thermostat damping.

Cool continuously from 4000 K to 300 K at 10 K/ps for 370 ps (370,000 steps), with pressure damping of 10,000 fs. Then hold at 300 K for 100 ps (100,000 steps), with pressure damping of 5000 fs. For example, use `fix cooling all npt temp 4000 300 100 iso 0 0 10000` and `run 370000`, then unfix cooling, define the hold integrator, and `run 100000`. Equivalent split runs that preserve the temperature schedule are allowed. Unfix each completed stage integrator before defining the next.

After the hold, reheat continuously from 300 K to 4000 K at 10 K/ps for 370 ps (370,000 steps), with pressure damping of 10,000 fs. Keep the 1 fs timestep and 100 fs thermostat damping throughout. The complete cycle requires 840,000 advancing steps, with boundaries at steps 0, 370,000, 470,000, and 840,000.

Record stage, step, elapsed time in ps, target and measured temperature, pressure, and density at sufficient resolution to reproduce the analysis, including each stage endpoint. Time and step count start at zero. Keep restartable states at the initial state, cooling end, hold start, and hold end, preserving the cell, atom IDs, species, positions, charges, velocities, and elapsed time. Save the input and raw log files. Carry the same system through all stages without replacing atoms or reinitializing velocities. Also retain reheating start and end states.

Assess the density response using measured temperature as the temperature coordinate; exclude measured temperatures above 2600 K from transition fitting. Choose and document the estimator, exact data ranges, evidence for distinct regimes, and sensitivity to fitting-window choices. Report each resolved cooling or reheating Tg and, when both are resolved, their signed difference (reheating minus cooling) in kelvin. Do not force a numerical intersection when a transition is not resolved: use method="unresolved", null for that Tg and for delta_tg_K, and retain the assessed data indices, explanation, and single-line residual sum of squares as shown in the unresolved example. An unresolved claim requires independent scientific review, not an invented Tg.

For the 300 K hold, report representative mean temperature and density, and quantify density drift using justified windows. Assess equilibration and the limitations from finite simulation time, rapid ramps, density fluctuations, and fitting sensitivity. A reproducible fitted breakpoint alone does not establish a physical glass transition.

Scoring verifies reproducibility and screens weak fits rather than requiring a particular Tg. For the built-in estimators, fewer than six distinct measured temperatures or a BIC gain below 6 over a single straight line leaves the transition check pending for scientific review; see the submission guide for the exact calculation. This screen does not establish statistical significance for correlated MD data.
submission_format: Submit the path to your completed manifest.json file. Use the blank example as a guide. Paths inside the manifest may be relative to the manifest file.
